judgments.reasoning_cat1: "One or more Committees" comprised of "two or more Trustees ... an equal number of Employer Trustees and Union Trustees" is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.10 defines a Committee as needing only "at least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee," which permits unequal composition — a direct inconsistency with 5.6(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prudent-person formula is statutory boilerplate; "unless, under the circumstances, it is clearly prudent not to do so" is a familiar ERISA qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It constrains a Board that Section 5.5 empowers "in its sole and absolute discretion" and that 5.9(b) purports to immunise for any act or omission; harmonising the three requires work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allowing Trustees to accept documents as "conclusive evidence" with "no duty to make any investigation" is broad but plainly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That no-inquiry protection is hard to square with 5.7's prudence duty and with 9.9's audit rights over Employer records.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (b) immunises Trustees for "any loss arising out of any act or omission" without qualification, while (d) carves out fraud, willful misconduct and gross negligence — the two subsections state different liability rules.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both are prefaced by "except as may otherwise be provided by ERISA," and 5.7's standard of care and 5.11's fiduciary insurance assume liability can exist, so the absolute language cannot be taken at face value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bonding obligation keyed precisely to ERISA § 412 with a discretionary top-up; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.3's expense provisions and 5.11; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mandatory purchase obligation qualified by "to the extent not precluded by ERISA"; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-reference to 5.9 is accurate and the two dovetail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deposit and signature-authority rules are stated concretely, with delegation to two Trustees, one from each side.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.15's last sentence separately allows Fund employees to sign checks on designated accounts, a parallel route that does not squarely conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Ministerial powers or duties" is the operative limit and its boundary against discretionary or fiduciary duties is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 5.5(r), 5.5(s) and 5.6 permit delegation of fiduciary responsibilities, so the ministerial-only limit in 5.13 is not the whole picture.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It confers "complete authority, in its sole and absolute discretion, to construe the terms of the Plan or this Agreement" with decisions "final and binding upon all parties affected" — language whose reach (does it bind employers? courts?) is regularly contested.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Finality here sits against 6.6's arbitration of Board deadlocks, 9.10's mandatory arbitration of withdrawal-liability claims, and 9.6/9.7's contemplation of judicial determination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Execution authority is spelled out with concrete alternatives; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.6 makes an instrument executed by the Chairman alone conclusive in favour of third parties, whereas 5.15's default requires Chairman and Secretary — a real inconsistency about who can bind the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The term of Fund officers shall commence on the date of their election" but no election procedure is prescribed anywhere in the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No election mechanism appears in Article 6 either, and 6.4 requires unanimity of units, so officer selection could deadlock into 6.6 arbitration; the gap is real but not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Special meetings may be called by the Chairman or Secretary or by any four Trustees" is clear in wording but sets a number close to the whole Board.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Under 3.1 there are five Trustees, and under Amendment No. 4's 3.1 only four, so "any four Trustees" would require unanimity to call a special meeting — an incoherence with the amended composition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence quorum rule stated in exact numbers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With only two Employer Trustees under 3.1 (and only two Union Trustees after Amendment No. 4), the quorum demands every Trustee, which cuts against 6.4(c)'s proxy scheme and makes 6.4(d)'s "lack of a quorum" route to arbitration the ordinary case.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It first says action requires a "unanimous vote of the Trustees" and then that action is by "unanimous vote of the two units" with each unit voting by internal majority — two different unanimity rules in one subsection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 10.1 and 10.3(a)(1) require a "unanimous vote of the Board," whose meaning depends on which of 6.4(a)'s two formulations governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; "need not be verbatim" is a clear relaxation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.1(b)'s recordkeeping duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deadlock-arbitration machinery is detailed, though the Chairman's duty to submit is mandatory while any single Trustee may instead petition the district court.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is invoked by 6.4(d) for deadlock, yet 6.6(a) describes only lack of unanimity or quorum; and 5.14 makes Board decisions final, which an arbitrator's substituted decision cuts across.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence — "Where the Administrator is a Trust Fund, subject to the terms of this Agreement ..." — is not a complete sentence and never states the Administrator's responsibility, so the operative predicate is missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (c) gives the Administrator "determinations as to benefit eligibility and amount," while 7.2(15)-(17) gives the same function to the Board and 5.14 reserves it exclusively to the Board — an allocation conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eighteen-item list closing with a general "exercise of those functions and responsibilities which the Board deems necessary and appropriate," a catch-all against enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Items (1) and (2) give the Board the right to amend or terminate the Trust and Plan "at any time," which conflicts with 10.1's unanimity and provisos, 10.2's absolute limits and 10.3(a)(2)'s Union/Association joint-resolution route.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation of appointment and segregation duties; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (c) duplicates 8.4(b)'s reservation of Section 5.5 powers to the Board where no manager is appointed; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete certificate, written-agreement and periodic-meeting requirements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-reference to 8.8 is accurate and consistent with 7.2(10) and 7.2(13).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Board may require" makes the fiduciary acknowledgment optional, in a sentence otherwise precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.18 makes a written acknowledgment of fiduciary status part of the very definition of "Investment Manager," so a manager appointed without one would fall outside the defined term — a genuine inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It excepts "subsections (3) through (y)" of Section 5.5 — a cross-reference to a subsection numbering that does not exist (5.5 runs (a) through (y)), so the scope of the manager's powers cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Investment Manager's "exclusive authority" over its account has to be squared with 5.5's grant of the same powers to the Board and with 8.1(c)/8.4(b); the mis-cite is what makes the boundary uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad exculpation opening with "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary," qualified by assets over which the Board "has specifically assumed investment management duties."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 7.2(13)'s duty to monitor and evaluate managers and 5.7's prudence standard, which assume some Board responsibility for manager selection and oversight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Order-issuance authority stated plainly and made subject to the management agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.4(a) and 8.8; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence making the manager's terms "the sole responsibility of the Board"; short but unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits oddly beside 8.5 and 8.8, which disclaim Board responsibility for the manager's acts, though the two address different things (appointment versus performance).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permissive "may (but need not)" guideline power and its non-acceptance disclaimer are clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.2(10) and 8.5's exculpation; nothing pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is entirely delegated to outside documents — "the amount required by the Collective Bargaining Agreements" — and the closing sentence disclaims any effect on those agreements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.8 conditions a CBA's status on being "acceptable to the Board" and 2.4(a) on Board approval, while 9.1 says nothing in the Trust Agreement alters any such agreement; contribution disputes turn on which controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Effective date and duration keyed directly to the CBA; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1 and 2.4(b)'s designation of a participation date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payee and manner of payment stated concretely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Fund name in 2.1 and the Preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A liquidated damage penalty equal to the greater of interest on, or twenty percent of, the unpaid contributions" is compressed, and calling it a "penalty" while framing it as liquidated damages invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sets interest "at a rate calculated in accordance with Section 9.5," but 9.5(b) states a flat rate rather than a calculation method and was itself rewritten by Amendment No. 2; 9.7 then repeats the same remedies for court awards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single bracketed list of recoverable items ending in "interest at a rate of 18 percent per annum" — the rate is flat, but whether it is a rate of interest or an unenforceable penalty, and whether it governs withdrawal-liability as well as contribution delinquency, are live on the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 2 replaced this very subsection with "18 percent per annum or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate," and 9.4(a) and 9.7(b)-(c) both cross-refer to a "method set forth in Section 9.5" that the flat-rate text does not supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines "unpaid contributions" by reference to this Agreement, any CBA or other agreement and "any rules or guidelines promulgated by the Board," a broad and partly self-referential definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The ERISA §§ 502(g)(2) and 515 remedies it invokes are echoed but not identically stated in 9.7's list; the two remedy schemes overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The five recoverable heads are enumerated, closing with "such other legal or equitable relief as the court deems appropriate" — a catch-all after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It computes interest "in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5," but 9.5(b) supplies a flat rate that Amendment No. 2 made discretionary, so the cross-reference no longer yields a determinate figure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional non-waiver saving clause, though it mixes "Article IX" and "Article 9" in the same sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves rights that 9.10 purports to channel exclusively into arbitration for withdrawal-liability claims — a modest tension in the same Article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All records deemed necessary by such persons" and an unconditional right to charge the Employer for the audit cost are one-sided and unbounded standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with 9.6's collection remedies and 7.2(9)'s delinquency procedures; no contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says withdrawal-liability claims "shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts ... but shall be subject to determination only by arbitration," then in its last sentence preserves the Fund's right to sue in court — the exclusivity is contradicted within the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That reservation also sits against 9.5(a) and 9.6, which authorise the Board to sue, and against 5.14's making Board determinations final and binding; which forum decides an assessment is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Amended, at any time and in any manner" is then cut back by three provisos, one of which ("not inconsistent with the purposes for which the Fund was established") is an open-textured standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(1)-(2) states the Board may amend or terminate "at any time" without those provisos, and 10.2 imposes a further absolute bar, so the amendment power is described three different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition is absolute but its carve-out — "except as otherwise provided in Section 10.3" — points to a section that itself forbids any reversion to an Employer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The provision that actually permits a return of contributions to an Employer is Section 4.4, not 10.3, and 10.3(b) says "under no circumstances" shall corpus revert to an Employer, so the cross-reference is misdirected and the exception empty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three termination triggers are enumerated clearly, though (b)'s "distribute or apply any remaining surplus in a manner consistent, in their opinion, with" the Agreement is a subjective standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its "under no circumstances" bar on reversion to any Employer contradicts 4.4's return-of-contribution power and empties 10.2's "except as otherwise provided in Section 10.3" carve-out; termination by Union/Association joint resolution also cuts against 7.2(1)'s Board-only power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recordkeeping duties are concrete, opening with a broad "unless otherwise delegated" qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.1(g)'s Administrator recordkeeping and 7.2(7)'s auditor coordination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such commercially acceptable valuation method or methods determined by the Board" leaves the method to the Board's own judgment, though tied to fair market value.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11.1(c) and 5.5(v)'s fair-market-value collateral test; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes situs as "the New York City metropolitan area" — an area, not an address — and then deems the Board located "at that address," a referent that does not exist in the sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.8 supplies actual addresses (later changed by Amendments 1 and 3), so the deemed location has to be sourced elsewhere; the friction is small.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard New York choice-of-law clause with an express ERISA-preemption carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.10 says arbitrations are governed by New York law "to the extent not superceded by ERISA," which matches; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2's reference to signature on "any counterpart or copy hereof."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard interpretive clause; the direction that the Agreement "shall not be construed by reference to" headings is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters most where a heading misdescribes the text — Section 3.8 is titled "Removal of Union Trustees" but governs who holds office — which this clause resolves rather than creates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence designating the Board as process agent; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.1's situs and 12.8's notice addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Third-party protection is stated in absolute terms — no duty to inquire and Chairman-executed instruments "conclusive" — a one-sided formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 makes the Chairman and Secretary jointly the executing officers, so treating a Chairman-only instrument as conclusive contradicts the Agreement's own execution rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Importing all Plan definitions "except as otherwise expressly provided herein" is workable but creates a two-source definitional regime.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 defines many of the same terms and 1.8's introductory clause adds "unless the context otherwise requires," so which source governs a contested term is not settled in one place.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice is "deemed duly given ... when deposited by first-class mail," and the Union address is given as 41-18 27th Street where every other reference is 47-18 — a transcription slip in an operative address.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names a "Fund Administrator" where Article 1 defines "Administrator," and Amendments Nos. 1 and 3 replace these addressees with a "Fund Director" at a different address, so the original text is superseded in part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision as transcribed begins mid-sentence with no subject, so the class of persons denied any right, title or interest cannot be identified from the text itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conditions all entitlement on a Board determination, which reinforces 5.14 but sits against 12.16's "except as set forth in the Plan" and against 4.2's Plan-based entitlements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-employment-right and no-equity clause, qualified by "except as set forth in the Plan."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out reopens what 12.15 closes absolutely, a small tension between neighbouring sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Continue in effect without limit as to time" is expressly made subject to Article 10, so the apparent perpetuity is qualified on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 10 and 7.2(1)-(2) supply the amendment and termination routes it refers to; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It recites that "the Plan is hereby amended" while the operative change is to Section 12.8(b) of the Trust Agreement — the wrong defined instrument is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Plan" and "Trust Agreement" are separately defined in 1.20 and 1.2, and 10.1 requires unanimous Board action to amend either; it also introduces a "Fund Director" title unknown to Article 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement text sets interest at 18 percent "or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate given [the] circumstance" — a rate that is simultaneously fixed and wholly discretionary, with no standard for choosing between them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(a) and 9.7(b)-(c) compute interest "in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5," and after this amendment that method is whatever the Trustees decide, which unsettles the court-award formula in 9.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean address-substitution amendment, though it states no effective date and the Association address is cut off mid-line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes 12.8(a)-(d) and Amendment No. 1, and continues the "Fund Director" label rather than the defined "Administrator."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A restated preamble listing four current Trustees; the stray "2. the following:" is a transcription artifact rather than a substantive defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It still equates "Fund" and "Plan" as one label despite 1.20 and 1.22 defining them differently, carrying forward the original preamble's tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence reads "The appointment of Trustees shall be selected by the provisions of Section 3.4" — a grammatical error replacing "governed," and 3.4 in any event covers only successor appointments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reducing the Board to two and two makes 6.3's quorum of two of each require every Trustee and makes 6.2(b)'s "any four Trustees" a unanimity requirement for calling a special meeting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare substitution of names; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with amended 3.1's two-and-two composition and with the amended Preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headed "Removal of Union Trustees" but stating only who serves ex officio, and "vice president/secretary treasurer" is an ambiguous compound office title.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves the same unresolved overlap as the original 3.8 with 3.10's designation-by-principal-officer route and 3.3(b)'s designation by the Union, and provides no removal mechanism to parallel 3.7's at-will removal of Employer Trustees.
